<!--
Confidentiality first: this repository is public. Do not name a customer, paste
tenant data, or describe an internal Microsoft tool or roadmap. Describe the
failure in general terms - that is enough to judge the proposal.

The most useful proposals come from something that went wrong more than once.
A topic that would be useful "for completeness" is the kind of skill this repo
deliberately does not write.
-->

## The failure

What actually went wrong, and what it looked like at the moment it went wrong.
Symptoms, not diagnosis.

## How often you have hit it

Once, a few times, every engagement? Say honestly. Once is still worth filing;
it just gets weighed differently.

## What you had to learn to get past it

The part that was not in the documentation, or was in the documentation but three
pages away from where you were looking.

## Which bucket

`build`, `connect`, `review`, `operate`, `deliver` or `learn` - named for what
the user is *doing*, never for the Microsoft product. If it does not fit one,
say so; that is useful information about the proposal.

## Who reaches for it, and when

Would an agent reach for this on its own from a description of the situation
(model-invoked), or would a human pick it deliberately from a list (user-invoked)?

## What already covers this

Microsoft documentation, an existing repo, or an existing skill here. If Microsoft
already solves it well, the right outcome may be a `registry/` entry that routes
to them rather than a skill - and that is a real contribution, not a rejection.
